transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-15
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Rossi (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood DevAdv), Anika Sharma (CTO, Noventa), Ben Carter (Lead Dev), Sofia Li (SRE), Marcus Rey (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, that's Luca our solutions engineer and Jordan who does developer advocacy for quickstarts, we'll walk through the Python and TypeScript SDK flows and cover auth, env setup, and then spend time on Optimize recommendations — batching and caching for your use case.

[00:18] Anika: Thanks, Maya. Quick context — Noventa is building a clinical intake assistant and we need to ship an MVP within 8 weeks. Main concerns: latency under 400ms for snips, PHI handling, and predictable cost.

[00:27] Luca: Got it. We'll show two flows — a fast path with the hosted Redwood API so you can iterate, and a Dedicated pilot for throughput and isolation. We'll also demo the Console so you can see token-level cost breakdowns.

[00:40] Ben: On the auth side we already have an internal secrets manager. We want to avoid keeping raw keys in CI, and we need SSO for the Console.

[00:47] Maya: Totally. Redwood supports API keys for dev and service usage, SAML SSO for Console, and integrations with KMS for key wrapping. We'll show examples.

[01:02] Jordan: I'll kick off with a quick Python quickstart link, then Luca will flip to the Console. Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/quickstart-py-ts (note that's the internal short link)

[01:20] Jordan: Example snippet — set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment, pip install redwood-sdk, then from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); response = client.generate('summarize: ...').

[01:35] Ben: Is the env var name standardized across languages? We have secrets automation that maps to names.

[01:42] Luca: Yes we recommend REDWOOD_API_KEY for parity, but the SDK accepts explicit keys too. For CI we advise using provider-specific secret refs (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager or GitHub Actions secrets) rather than writing to files.

[01:58] Sofia: For the SRE perspective, what about rotated keys and audit trails?

[02:04] Maya: Rotation is supported — you can create scoped API keys and rotate them; Console will show usage per token and per key. Audit logs are available in Private/Dedicated and via the Console's export for hosted customers.

[02:19] Marcus: Do you have HSM/KMS integrations? We run keys in our KMS and need server-side encryption.

[02:27] Luca: Yes, we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for hosted we have envelope encryption options and can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping — though that typically is in the Dedicated/Private conversation.

[02:45] [03:05] Jordan: Switching to the TypeScript quickstart — npm install @redwoodai/sdk, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, and use const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] });. We'll paste the sandbox repo link in the follow-up.

[03:25] Ben: Any differences in streaming support between py and ts?

[03:31] Luca: Both support streaming. The JS client has native event stream handlers in Node; Python has an iterator yield model. Some of the small naming bits are different, but behavior is the same. Small caveat: certain low-level configurations (kernel tweaks) are applied on the runtime side and surface via the Console & Optimize recommendations, not in the SDK API.

[03:58] Anika: Can you show the Console? We want to see cost breakdowns and route configs — and how to pin models for the pilot.

[04:06] Luca: Sure. I'm sharing my screen — heading to Console -> Projects -> noventa-pilot.

[04:20] [04:35] Luca: Here you can see per-route metrics: latency median/p95, token cost, and token counts. The traces show per-call token breakdown which helps you tune prompts. We also have route-level fallbacks. For example if your low-cost model is saturated it can fallback to a smaller or higher-latency model depending on policy.

[04:50] Sofia: Where is the KV cache shown? We saw reference in docs but not sure how to enable.

[04:58] Luca: In Console under Optimize -> Caching you can enable prefix caching and configure TTLs. For your use case we usually recommend prefix KV caching for static instruction prompts and conversation KV for session-level cache. It saves tokens and reduces latency. We will attach a suggestion doc.

[05:20] Jordan: Quick note about prompts: small template changes can reduce tokens dramatically. We'll share a prompt audit sample.

[05:32] Anika: How about quantized models — we want to keep accuracy for clinical data but lower cost.

[05:38] Luca: Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per model and workload. For clinical intent extraction we often keep fp16 or int8 with calibration to preserve performance. There's a tradeoff — we can show a perf vs quality chart from past pilots.

[05:55] Ben: Network topology — if we use Dedicated in a cloud region, can we route from our VPC?

[06:02] Maya: Yes Dedicated and Private offer VPC peering and private endpoints. For the Dedicated pilot we can set up a private endpoint so traffic doesn't traverse public internet — helps with compliance and latency.

[06:18] Marcus: For SOC 2 and logs we need exportable audit logs. Is that present in hosted?

[06:25] Luca: Hosted includes basic usage logs; Dedicated and Private provide richer audit logs and long-term retention options. We'll include the SOC 2 artifacts in the security packet.

[06:40] [07:00] Ben: We're also planning a CI pipeline — can you show a recommended pattern for CI secrets?

[07:07] Jordan: Recommended: store the REDWOOD_API_KEY in your secrets manager, mount it to the pipeline as an env var, restrict the key to a service role scope (read-only for inference), and use short-lived keys when possible. Avoid baking keys into images.

[07:28] Ben: Cool. Any examples for a GitHub Actions job?

[07:34] Jordan: Yes — we'll paste a sample in the follow-up. It uses secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY and a step that runs the SDK test harness.

[07:50] Anika: On billing and cost visibility, can we get token-level cost mapped to our product routes? We need to bill internal teams.

[07:58] Luca: Console gives per-route cost breakdowns and you can tag routes or projects. We can set up cost allocation tags so you can export to your billing system.

[08:12] [08:40] Maya: Let's demo a tiny end-to-end: a TypeScript microservice calling the SDK with streaming, versus a Python batch job using the generate API. Luca will run both so you can see latency differences.

[08:50] Luca: Running demo now — first, TypeScript streaming: initiating chat session… [09:01] looks like ~220ms on our region. Now Python batch for a 300-token summary returns ~480ms total because of model choice and sequence length — that aligns with the numbers we publish in the catalog for similar models.

[09:25] Ben: That streaming number is promising. Which model was that?

[09:30] Luca: That was redwood-alpha-small (example in pilot) with KV cache warm. For your clinical prompts we may use a larger variant; we'll suggest a config that hits the 300-400ms target.

[09:45] Sofia: How predictable is caching behavior for cold starts? We need to know warm-up times and implications for tail latency.

[09:52] Luca: Warm-up matters. That's where Dedicated's reserved capacity helps — you avoid cold starts by keeping warm workers. We also support pre-warming strategies via the API. We'll include recommended autoscale settings to minimize tail latency.

[10:12] Anika: For the pilot, can we get a 2-week Dedicated trial with a limited capacity to run benchmarks?

[10:19] Maya: Yes, we typically offer a short Dedicated pilot under a trial contract — we'll provision a small pool and work with you on benchmark scripts. Luca will provide the config.

[10:30] [10:45] Marcus: About data residency — patient data stays in our environment before sending to Redwood?

[10:51] Maya: Best practice is to PII-filter and redact client-side, or use Private deployment if you need absolute data residency. For hosted API we have contractual controls and optional Private options. We'll document the options in the security pack.

[11:05] Ben: Are there SDK linting or CI tests for prompts? We want to fail deployments if prompts regress token counts or quality.

[11:12] Jordan: We have a tiny eval harness example — you can run simple prompt tests in CI measuring token counts and model responses against golden outputs. We'll attach a repo with a pytest harness and a JS Mocha example.

[11:30] Luca: Also, our Optimize product includes a prompt set evaluation runner you can run against a baseline to catch regressions. It's not magic but helps detect quality drops when you change prompts or roll models.

[11:45] Anika: Great. Anything else on networking — egress costs or peering?

[11:52] Maya: Egress depends on region/provider; we'll include expected egress notes for your region in the follow-up. Dedicated can be located in the same cloud region to minimize egress.

[12:10] [12:30] Ben: For the code examples, can we get a snippet that uses the SDK with an async retry wrapper for transient 503s?

[12:37] Luca: Yes — standard patterns: exponential backoff and idempotency keys for request deduplication. We'll paste a sample function in the repo.

[12:50] Marcus: One concrete compliance ask — can Redwood run a security review with our infosec team?

[12:57] Maya: Absolutely. We'll schedule a security deep-dive; Jordan will be the contact for developer experience and Luca for architecture.

[13:10] Anika: Okay let's recap next steps.

[13:15] Maya: Recap — Redwood will: 1) send SDK quickstart repos and sample CI configs, 2) share SOC 2 and security artifacts, 3) provision a small Dedicated trial for benchmarking, 4) schedule a hands-on pairing session the week of Jan 27. Customer will: 1) pick test prompts and dataset subset, 2) provide compliance questions list, 3) confirm internal stakeholder availability.

[13:40] Ben: Thank you, that sounds good.

[13:46] [13:55] Maya: We'll email the links and action items after the call, and set a calendar invite for the workshop. Thanks everyone.

[14:00] [END]
